recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not re-add an 'other' code, and do not use FHIR-32812 to revert the current extensible CodeableConcept binding; any concern with that binding belongs to the later FHIR-43164 decision family.
issue_request: FHIR-32812 was a Published OO change request for R5 asking to remove the 'other' code from DeviceNameType and, if that meant no out-of-set name type could be conveyed, to consider relaxing Device.deviceName.type to an extensible CodeableConcept or Coding. The final resolution was Persuasive with Modification: remove 'other' in accordance with FHIR-20639, but do not make that value set extensible as part of this issue.
initial_application: The seed was applied through the FHIR-20639 change family rather than by a separately named FHIR-32812 source commit. Commit cae641cfad replaced DeviceNameType with registered-name, user-friendly-name, and patient-reported-name, removing old codes including other. Commit c4a95b2b91 updated the Device and DeviceDefinition name type short/definition text to the same three codes, and merge dc516986c5 is the commit cited from the Jira comments.
additional_context: The Jira comment that mentions FHIR-20369 appears to be a typo because FHIR-20369 is an unrelated LIVD markdown issue, while FHIR-20639 is the DeviceNameType replacement referenced by the resolution and OO minutes. OO minutes on 2021-10-11 and 2021-10-25 record removing 'other,' determining extensibility, and linking the seed to FHIR-20639. Later applied issue FHIR-43164 intentionally changed DeviceDefinition.deviceName.type and Device.name.type from required code to extensible CodeableConcept for R6, so the current extensible binding is later work-group intent.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The active DeviceNameType CodeSystem source contains only registered-name, user-friendly-name, and patient-reported-name; active Device and DeviceDefinition name type definitions list the same three codes and bind to that value set. fhir.ini lists Device and DeviceDefinition as active resources. The later extensible CodeableConcept binding was preserved because it belongs to FHIR-43164, not an unapplied part of FHIR-32812.
